adaptations: Application package identities and fields
Application initializes Profile templates; no upstream official catalog
No upstream product Profile normalization or retired bundle deletion
Strict application TypeScript and retained causes for safe IO errors
Redacted configuration parser diagnostics omit source buffers and raw causes
Compatibility checks distinguish runtime version from public SDK and framework versions
Shared CLI runner with deterministic signal, proxy and cross-process lock disposal
Profile HMR preserves upstream serialization/reconciliation, with configuration and module diagnostic redaction
Credential references are opaque identifiers, not ambient-secret discovery; contained listener diagnostics omit thrown data
POST-only bounded authentication exchange, session cookies tied to Host generation and protected temporary bootstrap file delivery
Bounded pending exchanges and API peer lifetimes, peer-scoped cancellation and deterministic Fetch reader cleanup
Source-based Host checks/test resolution and application-wide dependency discovery
Public Remote generator targets canonical SDK modules and the SDK JsonValue recursion root; compiler runtime pinned to upstream TypeScript 6.0.3
Public reflection contracts live in canonical SDK; registry Host/Client providers share implementation, observer failures omit thrown data
Remote compiler excludes the unused upstream Cordis-inspector catalog projection and product-specific generation instructions
Registry effects are paired to caller and provider fibers; provider unload drains root-owned entries and rejects cached mutation views without effect accumulation
Strict generated-only Remote dispatch, generic Context-scoped forwarded events, independent Connection and Gateway Client faces
Content-fingerprinted artifact replacement, generic single-subject event typing, strict Client result codecs, bounded Host/Client queues and redacted unknown listener rejections

Canonical public storage contracts, caller/provider-owned hub contributions, owned validated document domains and private SQLite records with cross-process unit leases; relational facts use a separate native SQL facet without KV conversion

Desktop authentication uses only a shell-created generation-bound verifier in the Host, rejects cookie/token-file exchange, and retains the independent Host/Origin fence; Web keeps its protected POST exchange

Client module graphs, lazy browser factories and static assets use Axterm metadata/globals, canonical SDK observables, independent Node/browser artifacts and redacted observer/reconciliation diagnostics
Public UI Slot/store definitions retain framework-neutral SDK observables; the private React 18 renderer owns mounting and binding; upstream DSH product/session test assemblies are not imported

Application-owned Web carrier seeds the exact shared browser identities, supplies the unchanged framework Loader a browser resolver, owns fail-closed boot cleanup and reports redacted activation failures

Pinned Electron RunAsNode boot uses the same exposed Node module internals as the unchanged Cordis Loader; package HMR uses the exposed native module binding with explicit warning and guarded shapes instead of unsupported native fingerprint guesses

Desktop static document and streaming proxy retain same-document boot, use shell-memory generation headers instead of cookies, reject foreign redirects and strip credentials before ownership decisions

Legacy dependency analysis uses source-first application aliases and treats the hash-checked framework as vendor; canonical public descriptors/error class and scoped implementation are factored without circular module dependencies
A bounded, caller/provider-owned typed Remote event selection registry replaces the upstream Agent/product catalog and is mounted in the real Profile so Client generations remain live

Owned subprocess capability and its local/Win32/lazy-loader dependency closure use Axterm identities and the existing PTY pin; public selected Host contracts, bounded output/disposal and actual caller/provider lifecycle integration follow ADR-070. Implementation is not accepted until native/source-free tests pass.
